newsitem.title: USA: US OPTIONS FOCUS/Expiration takes center stage.
newsitem.headline: US OPTIONS FOCUS/Expiration takes center stage.

text.p: Much of Thursday's major U.S. stock index volume was related to the expiration of June contracts at the end of the week, traders said.
In the S&P 100, put premiums were getting hit as the market moved higher but call premiums in the June series, at least, did not expand much.
The spot OEX was up 3.13 at 870.12 at about 1155 CDT/1655 GMT.
The at-the-money June 870 call, which was most active with volume of more than 8,640 contracts, was up 1/2 at 4-1/2.
The same put, which was the busiest OEX put with turnover of nearly 7,200 contracts, lost 2-1/4 to 3-3/8.
"Mostly put premiums are suffering here at the moment, but that's due to (market) direction, I think," said Jack Callahan, an independent market maker in the OEX.
The Dow industrial average was up 38 at 7,756.
Callahan said premiums remain high in the in-the-money calls and a lot of that could come out as they finish trading Friday and expire Saturday.
He added that most of the activity so far was related to the expiration.
Traders and analysts noted that open interest in OEX calls remains high, which is generally viewed as bullish.
"Call buyers have just simply bought them and held them. It seems that's why open interest is so big," Callahan said.
He added that with the sharp market swings experienced lately, "you can get a lot of bang for your buck in these expiring calls."
Lawrence McMillan, publisher of the Daily Volume Alert, said in a report Thursday that open interest also remains high in S&P 500 .SPX options and in June S&P 500 futures and futures-options.
He said if the investors holding those positions decide to convert them into stock instead of rolling them out to farther-dated contracts, the market could get a solid upside boost Friday morning.
June SPX options, futures and futures-options stop trading today and settle off the opening trade Friday.
The heaviest activity in SPX options was in the July 910 calls, which traded 14,325 contracts.
The June 900 calls traded more than 10,000 contracts and the June 865 calls traded about 7,900. The June 880 puts were the most active SPX puts, with turnover of about 6,500.

Jerry Hegarty, an options analyst at Thomson Financial Services, said in a report that both equity and index put and call buying were fairly even through the first half of Thursday's session, suggesting the market may struggle to post further gains today.
"On the other hand, the chances of a meaningful selloff are remote," he added.
